issues.description: Basic-usage example silently relies on insertion-order iteration to fetch the node, which is not the documented contract.
issues.detail: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` returns whatever node the Pipeline yields first. For a single-node pipeline this happens to work, but Pipelines generally sort or topologically order nodes, so a reader who copies this pattern into a larger pipeline will get the wrong node silently. Use `pipeline.nodes[0]` with a comment, or look up by `name=='train_model_node'`.

issues.description: Contract of `preview_fn` is never stated: signature, arity, return-type invariant, and error semantics are left to inference.
issues.detail: A literate treatment would open with: a preview_fn is a zero-argument callable returning a PreviewPayload subclass; it is invoked lazily by node.preview(); exceptions propagate to the caller. The reader currently has to reverse-engineer this from examples. One short paragraph before Basic Usage would make the rest of the document follow by deduction.

issues.description: "Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs" is asserted but never reconciled with the closure example that fakes it.
issues.detail: The closure pattern captures a literal `sample_data` defined at pipeline-construction time, which is not the same as accessing node inputs at run time. A careful reader will ask: what if the data only exists after the node runs? The doc should either show DataCatalog access inside the closure or explicitly say run-time input/output access is out of scope for this release.

issues.description: `ImagePreview` example has unreachable code after `return`, presented as if both branches were live.
issues.detail: The commented-out data-URI alternative sits below an unconditional return. It reads as a two-option example but is syntactically dead. Either split into two separate functions or move the data-URI form into a comment before the return so the example actually parses as intent.

issues.description: Several `node(...)` snippets are shown at module top level without a surrounding Pipeline, making them non-runnable as written.
issues.detail: The Mermaid-config and code-preview blocks end with a bare `node(func=..., preview_fn=...)` call that produces a Node but is not assigned or wrapped in a Pipeline. A reader copy-pasting will get an unused value and no pipeline. Wrap consistently or annotate `# inside Pipeline([...])`.

issues.description: Lowercase `polars` added to the Vale ignore list without explanation; capitalised `Polars` already exists.
issues.detail: This is a minor data-structure-of-the-style-guide question: the ignore list now contains both `Polars` and `polars`, which suggests the linter is case-sensitive but the doc only uses the lowercase form once in passing. Worth a one-line comment in the PR, or normalise to the capitalised brand name in prose and drop the lowercase entry.

review.summary: This is a documentation-only PR adding a how-to section for node `preview_fn`. Decision label: NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The prose is competent and the worked examples cover each preview type, but the document never states the contract of `preview_fn` up front (zero-arg callable, lazy invocation, return-type invariant) — every reader has to induce it from examples. A few code snippets are subtly non-runnable or misleading: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` assumes iteration order, bare `node(...)` calls dangle outside any Pipeline, and an `ImagePreview` example has unreachable code after `return`. The "no access to inputs/outputs" caveat is asserted and then partially contradicted by the closure example without reconciliation. None of this blocks merge, but the document would be markedly stronger with one paragraph defining the contract and a careful pass over the examples so they parse as intended.
